summary: Ordered plan for wiring the per-agent tool grant into the spawner. `src/engine/agents.ts` and the `--tools`/`--add-dir` wiring in `src/engine/spawner.ts` are already written and uncommitted; the gap is dedicated test coverage for I/O matrix items 9-13 (tests/engine.agents.test.ts and tests/engine.spawner.tools.test.ts do not exist yet). The plan verifies the existing wiring against AD-17/ADR-001/ADR-003, adds the two missing test files, then runs the suite.

decisions.question: Should the plan re-implement the grant wiring in src/engine/agents.ts and src/engine/spawner.ts?
decisions.answer: No — both already implement the wiring (resolveAgentGrant/grantFromRoster/toolsArgumentFor, AD1_REQUIRED_FLAGS carrying --add-dir and --tools, buildStepArgv requiring tools/addDir with no default). Plan steps verify this against the spec rather than redo it.
decisions.rationale: git status shows src/engine/agents.ts as an untracked new file and src/engine/spawner.ts as modified, both already containing the AD-17/ADR-001 wiring described in the story; re-planning their creation would duplicate completed work.

decisions.question: What is the actual remaining gap for this story's grant-wiring task (Task 4 / matrix 9-13)?
decisions.answer: Two test files named in the Code Map do not exist on disk: tests/engine.agents.test.ts and tests/engine.spawner.tools.test.ts. tests/engine.spawner.test.ts already covers the argv shape generically (via a fixtureGrant), but not the roster-refusal case, the Write-divergence-is-reported case, or the ADR001_REQUIRED_FLAGS-vs-ADR-001 enumeration assertion.
decisions.rationale: Glob confirmed these two files are absent, and the module doc comment in src/engine/agents.ts explicitly defers the recursive no-hardcoded-roster guard and the divergence-reporting assertion to tests/engine.agents.test.ts, and the AD1_REQUIRED_FLAGS test comment in tests/engine.spawner.test.ts explicitly defers the ADR-001 enumeration check to tests/engine.spawner.tools.test.ts.

plan.intent: Confirm src/engine/agents.ts's grantFromRoster/resolveAgentGrant/toolsArgumentFor/AgentGrantUnresolved fully satisfy AD-17 (no compiled-in phase-to-tools table anywhere under src/engine/) and ADR-003 (the roster entry is authoritative; a grant that diverges from ADR-003's table is passed through and reported via `elevated`, never silently corrected).

Confirm src/engine/spawner.ts's buildStepArgv requires `tools`/`addDir` with no default, that planFor resolves the grant via grantFor before building argv, and that both ADR001_REQUIRED_FLAGS and AD1_REQUIRED_FLAGS already name --add-dir and --tools.

Confirm STEP_PHASES carries `analysis` and `planning` (AD-28 enum widening) and that registry.ts registers step.analysis/step.planning so the spawner's schemaFor/getContract re-parse has something to validate against for those two phases.

Add tests/engine.agents.test.ts covering I/O matrix 9-11: a spawn for `analysis` carries --tools from the roster entry and --add-dir scoped to the worktree; a phase with no roster entry throws AgentGrantUnresolved naming the phase and the roster read, never a default grant; a roster entry granting Write to analysis passes Write through in argv while the AgentGrant's `elevated` names the divergence. Also add the recursive guard proving no structure under src/engine/ associates an agent id with a granted tool name, planting a violation in a fixture tree to prove the guard catches it.

Add tests/engine.spawner.tools.test.ts covering I/O matrix 12-13: assert ADR001_REQUIRED_FLAGS equals ADR-001's four required flags verbatim, assert AD1_REQUIRED_FLAGS contains every one of them, and assert missingRequiredFlags names --tools on an argv built without it.

Run the vitest suite including the two new files plus tests/engine.spawner.test.ts and tests/engine.roster.test.ts, confirming no regression and that the recursive no-hardcoded-roster guard fails on the planted violation and passes once it is removed.
